covers.quote: The basic parts of a report are:
a landing page (a cover for printed reports)
preliminary content (separate pages in printed reports)
the main part of the report
supporting information (endmatter).
The type of report will determine what to include and where.
All reports have a landing page or cover (if printed).

rules.quote: Create complete reports with a landing page, preliminary content, body and endmatter.
rules.specification: The page identifies the basic parts but says that report type determines what to include. It does not specify which report types can omit particular parts.
rules.violation_condition: A report is missing an applicable basic part: a landing page or printed cover, preliminary content, the main body, or supporting endmatter.
when: Use a cover instead of a landing page for a printed report.
Determine which parts are applicable from the type of report.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the introductory completeness instruction and its elaboration; missing parts are distinct from incorrectly ordered parts.

covers.quote: The basic parts of a report are:
a landing page (a cover for printed reports)

the main part of the report

rules.quote: Order the parts of the report
rules.specification: The list supplies the default sequence. The page also says report type determines placement, without specifying departures for particular types.
rules.violation_condition: The report's basic parts appear in a different relative order from landing page or cover, preliminary content, main body, and endmatter.
when: Check the relative order of parts that are present, rather than flagging a missing part under this rule.
Account for conventions specific to the type of report.
rules.why: The heading states an ordering check elaborated by its own list; it is not merely a grouping heading under G-1.

covers.quote: Electronic versions must be identical to printed versions

rules.quote: Australian Government reports published online should include the same information as a printed version.
rules.violation_condition: An online report differs in information from its printed version, or an electronic version subject to parliamentary printing requirements is not identical to its printed version.
when: A corresponding printed version exists.
For documents subject to parliamentary printing standards, the page makes identity between electronic and printed versions mandatory.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates version parity, with the stricter parliamentary requirement recorded as a condition.

rules.quote: Use these to give an overview of the report so people can decide if they want to download or read it.
rules.specification: The page does not specify how much overview information is sufficient to support the reader's decision.
rules.violation_condition: The landing page or printed cover lacks an overview that lets a reader judge whether to download or read the report.
when: Apply to the report's landing page, or its cover if printed.
rules.why: G-1 selects the actionable body instruction rather than making the broader section heading a second rule.

covers.prefix: l appendices, use a title page.
covers.quote: List the title of each appendix on the title page.
covers.suffix: The title page is usually a rig

tags.specification: The page does not define the number meant by ‘several’.
tags.violation_condition: A printed report with several appendices lacks an appendix title page listing the title of each appendix.

when: The printed report has several appendices.
rules.why: G-2 combines the appendix title page and its required list as one completeness check.

anchor.quote: Include an alphabetical list of shortened forms or abbreviations when these are useful for the user.

tags.specification: The page does not define when a list is useful. Alphabetical ordering is handled by the separate list-ordering rule.
tags.violation_condition: The report lacks a list of shortened forms or abbreviations where that list would be useful to its users.

when: A list of shortened forms or abbreviations would be useful to users.
rules.why: The need for a list is distinct from the ordering of an existing list; G-2 preserves the usefulness condition.

anchor.quote: List glossary items in alphabetical order.

covers.quote: an alphabetical list of shortened forms or abbreviations
covers.suffix: when these are useful for the u

tags.violation_condition: Entries in a glossary or list of shortened forms or abbreviations are not in alphabetical order.

when: Apply to glossary lists and lists of shortened forms or abbreviations that are present.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates the same alphabetical-order check for the two list types without duplicating the list-existence check.

anchor.quote: If the list is brief, include it in the preliminary content.
anchor.suffix: Do not incorporate the list of

tags.violation_condition: A brief list of shortened forms is placed outside the preliminary content.

when: The report has a brief list of shortened forms.
rules.why: G-2 retains brevity as the location trigger without inventing a threshold.

anchor.quote: Do not incorporate the list of shortened forms in the glossary.

tags.violation_condition: The list of shortened forms is incorporated into the glossary.

when: The report contains a list of shortened forms.
This exclusion is not limited to brief lists.
rules.why: This is a separate prohibition on combining components, not another condition of preliminary placement.

anchor.quote: Use a glossary to explain specialist or unfamiliar terms.
anchor.suffix: Don’t use a glossary if there i

covers.prefix: all number of terms to explain.
covers.quote: You can explain these in the main part of the report.

tags.specification: The page does not define a ‘small number’ or provide an audience-specific vocabulary for unfamiliar terms.
tags.violation_condition: A report with specialist or unfamiliar terms needing explanation lacks a glossary, other than where only a small number of terms need explanation.

when: Specialist or unfamiliar terms need explanation.
A glossary is not required for a small number of terms; these can be explained in the main body.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3 retain the small-number exception and its permitted alternative.

anchor.quote: Don’t use a glossary if there is a small number of terms to explain.
anchor.suffix: You can explain these in the ma

tags.specification: The page gives no numerical definition of a ‘small number’.
tags.violation_condition: A report uses a glossary for only a small number of terms needing explanation.

when: Only a small number of terms need explanation.
rules.why: This explicit prohibition can flag an unnecessary glossary; it is distinct from the absence of a needed glossary.

anchor.quote: Always place a bibliography after a reference list or endnotes if the report has both.

tags.violation_condition: A bibliography precedes a reference list or endnotes when the report contains both.

when: The report contains a bibliography and a reference list or endnotes.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the alternative preceding components as conditions of one ordering check.

anchor.quote: Split large reports into volumes

covers.quote: Digital and printed reports can work better in volumes if they are large.
covers.suffix: Create a volume at a suitable p

tags.specification: The page does not define ‘large’ or when a report would work better in volumes. The body presents the division as beneficial rather than universally mandatory.
tags.violation_condition: A large report remains a single volume where division into volumes would improve its use.

when: The report is large.
Apply to digital and printed reports.
rules.why: G-4 reads the heading with its qualifying body text, preserving the recommendation rather than inventing a size limit.

anchor.prefix: r in volumes if they are large.
anchor.quote: Create a volume at a suitable point in the text.

tags.specification: The page does not define suitable breakpoints.
tags.violation_condition: A volume boundary falls at an unsuitable point in the text.

when: The report is divided into volumes.
rules.why: The location of a volume break is a different check from whether to divide a large report.

anchor.quote: Each volume should have a summary list of the contents of the other volumes in the set.
anchor.suffix: The index can be in each volume

tags.violation_condition: A volume lacks a summary list of the contents of the other volumes in its set.

when: The report has multiple volumes.
rules.why: This is a specific cross-volume contents requirement; optional index placement creates no additional rule under G-3.

anchor.quote: Number the pages according to the break in the volumes:

covers.quote: When the break is in the main body of the text, continue the numbering across volumes.
When the break is for different material (for example, endmatter), number each volume in a separate way.
Page numbering for the endmatter continues from the main body of the report.

tags.specification: The continuation requirements are explicit. For volumes of different material, the page requires numbering ‘in a separate way’ but does not prescribe the exact scheme.
tags.violation_condition: Page numbering restarts across a volume break within the main body, fails to use separate numbering for a volume of different material, or restarts at ordinary endmatter within a printed volume.

when: Continue numbering across a volume break in the main body.
Use separate numbering when the volume break separates different material, such as endmatter.
In a printed report, endmatter in the same volume continues the main body's pagination.
Preliminary pages have their own numbering conventions.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates pagination continuity and its volume-boundary cases, avoiding conflicting findings for endmatter in a separate volume.

anchor.quote: Always number preliminary pages per volume.

tags.violation_condition: Preliminary-page numbering in a printed volume continues the preliminary-page sequence from another volume instead of being numbered separately for that volume.

when: The printed report has multiple volumes with preliminary pages.
rules.why: This separately checks preliminary pagination per volume, not main-body continuity or the form of roman numerals.

anchor.quote: Where numbering restarts for each volume, references should include both the volume and page number.
anchor.suffix: Where the numbering continues a

covers.prefix: oth the volume and page number.
covers.quote: Where the numbering continues across volumes, use just the page number for the reference.

tags.violation_condition: A page reference omits the volume number when pagination restarts per volume, or includes a volume number when pagination continues across volumes.

when: Apply to references in printed multi-volume reports.
With restarted pagination, include both volume and page number.
With continuous pagination, use only the page number.
rules.why: G-2 treats the pagination scheme as the condition determining one reference-format check.
